text:
Maria (infra): heads-up — us-west2 AZ-C has a scheduled rack thermal maintenance tomorrow 03:00-05:00 UTC. They'll drain ~6 racks for firmware+fan swaps.
Jon (sre): thanks. any expected impact to dedicated slices or soft-affinity tenants?
Maria (infra): likely a couple of dedicated slices will get evicted/reshuffled during drain. noisy-tenant spillover last time created a tail in p50->p99 for a handful of customers. want to propose a brief routing fallback to preemptible warm-pool with prefix-preserve so KV cache can be rehydrated quickly.
Kai (platform): we can do prefix-preserve for top models, but we should avoid routing heavy embedding jobs to preemptible (they thrash kvcache). Suggest model-based routing: gen/chat -> warm-preemptible with cache stitch; embeddings -> keep on dedicated if capacity.
Ashley (product): FYI this impacts some enterprise customers (dedicated SLA). We should surface this in console banner + send an automated email to affected tenants.
infra-oncall: current dedicated utilization in us-west2 is 72% across AZs. preemptible warm-pool headroom ~18%. If we shift 3 dedicated slices, we should be ok but need to watch egress caps.
sre-bot: [telemetry] recent tail-latency spikes from previous AZ-C drain: p99 gen latency +320ms for tenant:acme-co (link: https://telemetry/redwood/ta/azc-drain-2025).
Jon (sre): cost-wise this will bump preemptible token spend a bit. can we limit fallback window and use a canary first?
Maria (infra): agreed — canary plan: pick 5 non-critical slices (top-5 warm tenants by traffic) move them at 02:50 for 30m, monitor p50/p95/p99 and kv-rehydrate rate. rollback if p99 increases >20% or error rate >0.5%.
Kai (platform): add a routing weight tweak instead of hard move: set weight 0.2 to preemptible for canary so traffic still mostly hits dedicated. If metrics OK, ramp to 1.0 for the 3 slices.
Ashley (product): add console banner + customer email draft. I can handle messaging if you send impacted tenant list.
infra-oncall: I'll run the canary and own rollback. Please ping me when routing config is ready.
Maria (infra): command we plan to run for the canary (dry-run flag first):
```
routerctl route set --slice-id=slice-879 --target=preemptible-warm --weight=0.2 --prefix-preserve=true --dry-run
```
Jon (sre): tack on a short-lived QoS tag for canary to avoid noisy-eject: `qos=az-maint-canary`
Kai (platform): +1. Also add `max-egress=200mbps` to prevent egress burst.
infra-oncall: doing a quick capacity check now. If anything looks tight I'll request a burst quota from the region team.
Maria (infra): ops timeline: 02:30 - prefill preemptible warm-pool; 02:45 - run dry-run; 02:50 - canary weight=0.2; 03:15 - evaluate; 03:20 - full shift if green; 03:50 - revert to normal after drain completes.
Ashley (product): :eyes: I'll prepare comms. Who's oncall during rollback window (03:15-04:00)?
Jon (sre): I'm oncall that night and will shadow infra-oncall for rollback.
Maria (infra): perfect — tagging @eng-platform for visibility and @sales-eng for heads up to big customers. Kai can you add a quick dashboard (canary tv) with p50/p95/p99, error rate, and kv-rehydrate-rate?
Kai (platform): will push a minimal dashboard now, ETA 25m.
infra-oncall: confirmed routing dry-run succeeded in staging. moving to production with dry-run now and will update once we flip canary.
Maria (infra): :shipit: thanks everyone. keep chatter here for any anomalies.
Jon (sre): if we see NVLink errors or host thermal flaps, escalate to hw-maint immediately. last time those correlated with slab churn.
Maria (infra): noted. I'll drop a short post-drain checklist here (eviction logs, kvcache-miss heatmap, tenant latencies).
sre-bot: [deploy-bot] routerctl change applied by infra-oncall at 2025-11-06T02:50:12Z (change-id: r-azc-20251106-1).
